title: settings.json allows kbgit.py publish and git push to a headless agent with no prompt
goal: The permission rules of .claude/settings.json let a headless agent neither publish nor push off main without a prompt: `Bash(python3 _tools/kbgit.py *)` and its PowerShell twin are replaced by the subcommands a runner needs (sync, check-trailers, check-lanes, lane, fix --check and the read-only ones), `Bash(git -C *)`, `git checkout *`, `git branch *`, `git worktree *` and `git fetch *` are narrowed to the forms the runner uses, and permissions.deny names `kbgit.py publish`, `git push`, `git -C * push`, `git branch -D`, `git worktree remove` and `git checkout --` (Bash and PowerShell); the settings_allow_headless_runner test asserts the narrow allows and the deny rules, with a planted failure for each; found by the SP-4xngzagf review: `kbgit.py *` covers `publish` and `publish --rewrite` (a force push to the public home) and `git -C * push`, with deny holding only the two submit_feedback tools

run: import json,sys;p=json.load(open(".claude/settings.json"))["permissions"];a=p.get("allow",[]);d=p.get("deny",[]);sys.exit(0 if "Bash(python3 _tools/kbgit.py *)" not in a and any("kbgit.py publish" in x for x in d) and any("git push" in x for x in d) and "Bash(git -C *)" not in a else 1)

repro_reason: a permission decision is made by Claude Code when a tool call is attempted and no repro here can run one; the defect is the allow and deny lists of the configuration, so the repro reads them
